explanation: I has a singularity at x=t, and its partial derivative behaves like |x-t|^{-4/3}, which is not integrable there. II and III have continuous integrands and continuous partial derivatives: -2tx/(1+t²)² and -1/(1+x+t)², respectively. Their denominators never vanish on the stated domains, so differentiation under the integral sign is valid for II and III only.
